messages:
Maria Chen: hey team — quick design review: thinking about an "express invite" path when admins send invites to multiple users with the same role. mock in Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/XYZ. goal: reduce clicks and make keyboard first. Jon Patel: saw the mock, nice. my main worry is discoverability of SSO enforcement per-invite. can we show a small SSO badge next to role presets? :thinking_face: Elaine Rodriguez: +1 on badge. also a11y: ensure role presets are announced when focus lands. maybe use aria-live for the toast that confirms role selection. Sam Kaur: quick copy thought — instead of "Invite as: Role", try "Assign role" (shorter, clearer). also label the fallback when SSO required: "SSO required — user will be redirected to sign in" Alex Li: flow nit — current mock has role chips that expand into permissions. keyboard testing: focus order jumps from email field to role edit modal. we should keep inline role selection to avoid modal. Rachel Gomez: agree with inline. from PM side, we need telemetry events: invite.express.used and invite.role_preset.selected so we can measure uptake. cc @design-bot for event spec. design-bot: suggested events posted: invite.express.used, invite.role_preset.selected, invite.sso_override.attempted. see https://redwood.co/events/INV-45 Maria Chen: accessibility snippet proposal: use role list as a radiogroup for single role, and a checkbox-group for multiple roles. announce selection with aria-describedby pointing to a helper id that updates. sample: ```html
Role: Dev. SSO: Enabled ``` Jon Patel: that looks good. just ensure contrast for the focus ring — we saw issues in low-contrast theme. link to contrast check: https://contrastchecker.example.com/123 Elaine Rodriguez: copy tweak for the invite confirmation modal: change "You invited X people" -> "Invites sent — X recipients" (verb-first helps screen readers). Sam Kaur: usability test note: during prototyping, users missed the "manage role presets" link. maybe put presets in the left rail under "Quick actions" so it's discoverable. Alex Li: small UX edge-case: if invite fails due to SSO policy, we should surface which user and which policy blocked the invite. propose inline error: "Invite blocked by SSO policy for example@acme.com — requires SSO-enabled account" Rachel Gomez: can the UI show a one-click remedy: "Resend with SSO enforcement" button? product would love that. Maria Chen: yep, add a secondary action in the failure toast. I'll update the figma and push a new iteration. leaving a11y checkboxes for Elaine and Sam to review. Elaine Rodriguez: I can run a quick keyboard + NVDA pass tomorrow. Sam Kaur: I'll patch the copy in the propose branch and add aria attributes. PR to follow: https://github.com/redwood-inference/web/pull/4123 Alex Li: leaving a tiny CSS note — avoid using outline: none; use visible outline fallback for focus. Maria Chen: thanks everyone. let's reconvene after the PR review. :thumbsup:
